en.title: MGM+ Horror Hit 'From' Finally Lands on Netflix US This Fall
en.summary: Fans eager to dive into the chilling mysteries of **From** will soon have a new way to catch up. The acclaimed MGM+ sci-fi horror series is officially set to stream on Netflix in the United States for the first time.
en.body:
Prepare to be trapped all over again. The critically acclaimed MGM+ sci-fi horror series **From**, a show that masterfully blends existential dread with creature-feature scares, is making its way to Netflix in the United States for the very first time. This move is a significant one for fans who have been clamoring to experience the enigmatic town where no one can leave, and nightfall brings unspeakable horrors.

Starting Monday, October 19th, 2026, viewers will be able to stream the first four seasons of **From** on Netflix US. This limited-time licensing window offers a prime opportunity for new audiences to discover the series and for existing fans to refresh their memories before the show's fifth and final season premieres on MGM+ in 2027. Created by **John Griffin** and executive produced by genre heavyweights **Jeff Pinkner** and **Jack Bender** (both instrumental in the success of **Lost**), **From** centers on the residents of a mysterious middle American town that ensnares anyone who enters. Escape is an illusion, and as darkness descends, the town's true, terrifying nature is revealed.

## A New Home for Nightmares

This isn't **From**'s first dance with Netflix. Globally, the series was initially slated for distribution as a Netflix Original before a deal shifted. It later appeared as a licensed title in several international markets in April 2024, featuring only its first season, and has since departed those regions. The upcoming Netflix US debut represents a much broader, concentrated promotional push. By dropping the bulk of the series onto the world's largest streaming platform months before its ultimate conclusion, Amazon MGM Studios is employing a proven strategy to cultivate a larger fanbase and ensure maximum awareness for the series finale. This is a smart play to capitalize on the binge-watching culture and convert casual viewers into dedicated fans invested in unraveling the town's many secrets.

## The Stakes Are Higher Than Ever

For the dedicated **From** community, this Netflix expansion is a cause for celebration and a crucial step in the show's journey. It means wider accessibility for a series that thrives on shared theories and passionate discussion. The cliffhangers and intricate lore of **From** have fueled countless online conversations, and this move ensures that the conversations around the show's mysteries—who are the creatures, what is the nature of the town, and will anyone ever escape?—will reach an even larger audience. With the fifth and final season on the horizon, this Netflix rollout is designed to build an unprecedented level of anticipation, making the series finale an event.

## What's Next for the Survivors

Fans can mark their calendars for October 19th, 2026, when the first four seasons of **From** will be available on Netflix US. The exact duration of this licensing window has not yet been announced. Meanwhile, the fifth and final season is slated to premiere on MGM+ in 2027, bringing the gripping saga of **From** to its ultimate, and presumably terrifying, conclusion.

content_raw: Picture: MGM+ One of the biggest genre hits of the last few years is heading to Netflix in the United States. We can report that the MGM+ sci-fi horror series From will be streaming on Netflix US beginning Monday, October 19th, 2026, as part of a limited-time licensing window. We’re expecting the first four seasons of the show to land on the 19th, giving new viewers plenty of time to catch up ahead of the show’s fifth and final season, which is set to premiere on MGM+ in 2027. It’s the latest in a string of titles Amazon MGM Studios has sent over to Netflix in recent years, and it’s a fairly clear promotional play. Dropping the back catalog on the world’s biggest streamer a few months before the final season arrives is a tried-and-tested way to grow an audience or at the very least, awareness, and Netflix has been a launchpad for countless “second-window” hits in the past. This isn’t From’s first time on Netflix. When the series was first announced in 2021, Netflix was lined up to distribute it outside the US as a Netflix Original . That deal never materialized in the way it was planned, and the show instead arrived on Netflix as a licensed title in April 2024, landing in at least nine countries including the Netherlands, Belgium, Hungary, Poland and Sweden, as well as across the Middle East and North Africa. Only season 1 was ever made available in those regions, and the show has since departed. We can only see the show licensed to Netflix US, but we’ll update you if that changes.  What is From about? Created by John Griffin and executive produced by Jeff Pinkner and Jack Bender ( Lost ), From follows the residents of a nightmarish town in middle America that traps everyone who enters. Escape appears impossible, and when night falls, terrifying creatures emerge from the surrounding forest. Harold Perrineau leads the cast as Boyd Stevens, the town’s de facto sheriff, alongside Catalina Sandino Moreno, Eion Bailey, Scott McCord, Hannah Cheramy, Simon Webster, Ricky He and Elizabeth Saunders. The show premiered on Epix (now MGM+) in 2022 and has since become the most-watched series in the network’s history. When will From season 5 be on Netflix? Don’t count on it anytime soon. Season 5 went into production in Halifax, Nova Scotia, on July 6th, 2026, and is scheduled to wrap on November 27th, 2026, ahead of a 2027 premiere on MGM+. MGM+ confirmed back in April 2026, just days before season 4 debuted, that season 5 will be the show’s last. Amazon MGM’s growing relationship with Netflix When Amazon bought MGM for $8.45 billion back in 2021 , the expectation was that MGM’s library would gradually dry up on Netflix in favor of Prime Video. For a while, that’s what happened, with the likes of Stargate SG-1 and Fargo departing. That’s changed considerably since. Amazon MGM has been licensing to Netflix regularly again, most notably in the deal that brought the James Bond collection to Netflix alongside Rocky , Creed , Legally Blonde and Prime V
